stories.headline: Opposition to march to Election Commission on October 6; INDIA bloc demands return to ballot paper
stories.title: Opposition to march to Election Commission on October 6; INDIA bloc demands return to ballot paper
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: ‘Save Democracy’ marches involving youth groups and NGOs will be conducted across the country from October 2 to 8.

New Delhi: Announcing a comprehensive joint action plan over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) controversy, the INDIA bloc on Wednesday declared that it will hold nationwide rallies and 'save democracy marches,' with Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge stating that all member parties unanimously agreed elections must revert to paper ballots instead of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs).

The opposition coalition made the announcement following a three-and-a-half-hour strategy meeting attended by top leaders, including Kharge, former Congress presidents Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi, TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, RJD’s Tejashwi Yadav, and NCP(SP) MP Supriya Sule.
Addressing a joint press briefing after the meeting, Kharge outlined the roadmap agreed upon by the bloc.

As part of the agitation, "save democracy" marches involving youth groups and NGOs will be conducted across the country from October 2 to 8, alongside demonstrations outside district magistrate offices.
On October 6, all opposition MPs will march in protest to the Election Commission.
Furthermore, Leaders of the Opposition plan to seek an appointment with the President of India in the second week of October to submit a formal representation against "the vote chori government".
"We will hold a five big rallies and a date and place of which would be decided.
We will tell people how the government is snatching the right of the people to elect their government for running the country," Kharge said.
Drawing a parallel with previous economic policies, Kharge added: "Now everyone is realising that what Rahul ji was saying is correct and it is attracting attention.
First Prime Minister Narendra Modi did 'notebandi' now doing 'votebandi', taking away people's rights."
Kharge also stated that INDIA bloc leaders appeal to the Supreme Court that it should expedite the cases of SIR and electoral malpractices.

stories.headline: RBI MPC meet: Why your borrowing costs may go up from October
stories.title: RBI MPC meet: Why your borrowing costs may go up from October
stories.summary: High oil prices and weak monsoon, which will weigh on food prices, are likely to push up inflation, and in this backdrop, RBI may raise the repo rate by 25 bps each in October and December, feels D. K. Joshi, Chief Economist at Crisil
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'repo rate' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: "Monetary policy is on the verge of turning.
We are anticipating one rate hike in October and possibly another in December," said D. K. Joshi, chief economist at Crisil.
Risks are evolving, and some of them are becoming part of the baseline, he noted.
"You will have to incorporate monsoon and slightly higher prices somewhere in the outlook.
From an inflation point of view, in supply shocks, there is some persistence developing," said Joshi.
Inflation had already been on an upswing.
As per the latest available data, CPI (consumer price index) inflation rose 4.82% in August from 4.45% in July.
In the same period, food inflation increased to 5.95% from 5.52%.
Inflation is expected to rise given crude oil prices have shot up again in recent weeks.
More importantly, deficient rainfall will weigh on farm prices in the coming months, which will also exert upward pressure on inflation.
According to the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD), as of September 28, rainfall deficit in the country had been 12%.
Additionally, reservoir levels have also fallen below the decade-long average, which will have a bearing on the winter crop.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Rebukes UP Police Over FIR Discrepancies, Summons Officer
stories.title: Supreme Court Rebukes UP Police Over FIR Discrepancies, Summons Officer
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today(September 30) criticised the Uttar Pradesh police for registering a first information report against an unknown person in a case of motorcycle theft, despite the fact that the complainant had apprehended the thief on the spot.

In a case before Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva, the complainant appeared in person and alleged that despite him informing the UP Police about the person who stole his motorcycle, the police registered an FIR and left the column for adding the name of the accused person blank.
He stated that it was only after she approached the Allahabad High Court that the police added the name of an unknown person as accused.
The complainant ultimately had to knock on the doors of the Supreme Court.
When the matter came up here, the Court had asked the UP Police to file an affidavit in this regard, which was filed by Shobit Kumar, Circle, Khurja, Bulandshahr, UP.
However, the Court found the affidavit to be "utterly uninspiring" because it clearly revealed the FIR was supplemented with the accused's name later.
Questioning how an investigating agency could break the trust of the people, Justice Kumar asked the Circle Officer to be present in the next hearing.
"We find the affidavit dated 25.09.2026 filed by Mr. Shobhit Kumar, Circle Officer, Khurja, Bulandsahr, Uttar Pradesh, to be utterly uninspiring.
The said officer shall be present before this Court on the next date of hearing to account for the same.

It would be open to him to file a better affidavit explaining as to why First Information Report No. 195/2026 was registered on 19.08.2026 against an unknown motorcycle rider when it is the admitted fact that the said motorcycle rider was apprehended at the spot.
In paragraph 6 of the aforestated affidavit, the name of the motorcycle rider is disclosed as Tushar s/o Sh.
Prempal.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Rules Out Complete Firecracker Ban, Proposes Approach Balancing Sentiments & Health
stories.title: Supreme Court Rules Out Complete Firecracker Ban, Proposes Approach Balancing Sentiments & Health
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today indicated that it would not impose a complete ban on firecrackers or permit their unrestricted use, emphasising the need to balance religious sentiments with the adverse impact of air pollution on children, elderly persons and those suffering from illnesses.
“We make it very clear.
Neither we are going to agree with you for total ban.
Nor we are going to allow them to do it 24 hours.
For two reasons.
Total ban will have some sentimental effect, number one.
Number two, allowing them throughout the day will have a huge impact on every other living beings including old people, sick people and the children.
We need to find a solution whereby we can give specified time and we can specify what are the crackers to be used”, Justice MM Sundresh said.
A bench of Justice MM Sundresh and Justice Augustine George Masih was hearing the long-pending Arjun Gopal.
Union of India case filed by three infants highlighting the health hazards caused by firecrackers and seeking restrictions to curb air pollution.

Today, the Court considered the Union Government's proposal to permit the manufacture of joint firecrackers, subject to specified conditions, and the use of barium in green firecrackers, subject to further environmental testing.
The Court accepted the government's recommendation to allow new generation joint firecrackers subject to restrictions on the number and size of shells and the time interval between successive bursts.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Special Bench Criticises Manner Of CAPF Contempt Case Listing; Centre Says Request Was Made Before CJI
stories.title: Supreme Court Special Bench Criticises Manner Of CAPF Contempt Case Listing; Centre Says Request Was Made Before CJI
stories.summary: Justice Misra observed that the original bench ought to have been informed about the mentioning made before the CJI.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Justice Misra observed that the original bench ought to have been informed about the mentioning made before the CJI.

At the outset, Senior Advocate Shyam Divan, appearing for the petitioners, objected to the manner in which the matter had been listed before the special bench, saying no notice had been given to them about the request for listing the matter before another bench.
The bench perused a report submitted by the Registry explaining why the matter was not listed before the bench hearing the contempt petition on Tuesday.

The report stated that counsel representing the respondents (Centre) in both the contempt and writ petitions (challenging the CAPF Act) had mentioned the matters before the CJI for listing them before one bench, since one of the defences in the contempt proceedings involved the Act whose vires had been challenged in the connected writ petitions.
For context, the contempt petitions were before the bench of Justice Bhuyan (who authored the May 2025 judgment), and the writ petitions before Justice Misra's bench.
Divan questioned the procedure, saying, "You cannot have a listed matter plucked off the board.
This is an all India court.
People make travel arrangements and come here from all over the country.
Once it's listed why should it be removed?"
Justice Misra observed that the judges too had been informed only late on Tuesday night, at around 9 pm, that the special bench had been constituted.
Divan said the Registry could have remained present to explain the development and argued that a publicly notified matter should be taken up as listed.

Senior Advocate Guru Krishna Kumar, also appearing for the petitioners, said that no request for listing with the writ petitions had been made when the contempt petition was heard on September 22 and that there had been no such indication on Tuesday either.
